Title: Early planting with drought-tolerant maize varieties
Description: Plant drought-tolerant maize varieties (SC 719, SC 649) immediately after first effective rains (November 15-30) for optimal yield in Southern Province.
ApplicableConditions: Rainfed agriculture in agro-ecological region I and IIa, sandy loam to clay loam soils
ImplementationSteps: 1. Prepare land in October. 2. Plant within 7 days of first effective rains. 3. Apply basal fertilizer D-compound at 200kg/ha. 4. Thin to 2 plants per station at 2 weeks. 5. Top dress with Urea at 6 weeks.
ExpectedBenefit: 32% yield increase over local varieties, from 2.5 t/ha to 3.3 t/ha
AdoptionRate: 45% of farmers in Namwala adopted in 2025 season

Title: Maize-cowpea intercropping for improved soil fertility
Description: Intercrop maize with cowpea (2:1 ratio) to improve nitrogen fixation, suppress weeds, and provide additional protein-rich grain.
ApplicableConditions: Smallholder farms with <2 ha, suitable for all soil types in Southern Province
ImplementationSteps: 1. Plant maize at 90x50cm spacing. 2. After 2 weeks, plant cowpea between maize rows at 60x20cm. 3. Apply 150kg/ha D-compound at planting. 4. No nitrogen top dressing needed for intercropped maize.
ExpectedBenefit: 22% higher total productivity (maize equivalent), improved soil nitrogen, additional protein source
AdoptionRate: 35% of farmers in trial area adopted
